reader_question: What kinds of homes were finished each year?
grade_line: Documented: a Census Bureau survey of new construction
title: Builders finished 591,700 homes in buildings of five or more units in 2024, more than in any other year from 2000 to 2025.
measure_line: New privately owned housing units completed, thousands, by the number of units in the building, United States, 2000 to 2025. The chart starts in 2000 so each year’s column stays wide enough to read.
notes: Builders finished 1,626,900 homes in 2024: 1,018,600 in one-unit buildings, 16,600 in buildings of two to four units and 591,700 in buildings of five or more, 36 percent of the year’s homes and the largest share from 2000 to 2025.

The Census Bureau’s series starts in 1968. In 1972, 1973 and 1974 builders finished more homes in buildings of five or more units than in 2024, the most in 1973, 779,800, and the share was last higher in 1974, at 40.1 percent.
Homes in buildings of two to four units made up 0.6 to 1.8 percent of each year’s total from 2009 to 2025, too few to draw as more than a seam; the table gives each year.
alt: Stacked columns of new homes finished each year from 2000 to 2025, split into one-unit buildings, buildings of two to four units and buildings of five or more. One-unit homes make up most of every year; homes in buildings of five or more units reached 591,700 in 2024, the most of any year in the chart and 36 percent of the year’s 1,626,900. Two to four units shows as a thin seam from 2009 on.

table.caption: New homes finished by units in the building, thousands, 2000 to 2025

chart_notes: The parts stack from the zero line: one-unit buildings, then two to four units, then five or more, each named beside the last column, or in a key on a phone. Totals, in thousands of homes, print over 2006, 2011 and 2024, and 2024’s five or more units, 591.7, prints beside its part.
